name: Bampton (poll tax commissioner)
role: Royal poll tax commissioner for Essex
description: The royal commissioner whose attempt to collect unpaid poll tax at Brentwood on 30 May 1381 triggered the violence that began the revolt. His first name is given inconsistently across secondary accounts -- 'John' and 'Thomas' both appear -- and at least one careful modern review of the commission records has questioned whether a Bampton by either name actually held a formal seat on the Essex poll tax commission at all. This book treats the exact identity and formal role of the Brentwood commissioner as a genuine, unresolved gap in the record rather than asserting a first name or a title the documentary record does not clearly support.
narrative_function: The tax administration's face at the revolt's first flashpoint -- and an explicit example of how even the best-known 'first domino' of a famous event can rest on shakier documentation than the popular telling assumes.
